messages.author: f532f98b3e9b7d93
messages.subject: mirtCluster() in Linux
parts:
Hi Phil,

I'm using mirtCluster() on a Linux machine with 48 cores. It seems that the function is not working properly or not working at all. My simulation analysis takes about 10 minutes on a 8 core Windows machine but similar analysis takes more than 20 minutes on the Linux. Could you please help me on this? FYI, I tried ordinary R and Microsoft Open to see if mirtCluster() would work differently but it was the same.

Thanks,
Amin.

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: mirtCluster() in Linux
parts:
That sounds strange. Could you provide something reproducible? Also for future reference, in simulations I'd generally recommend avoiding mirtCluster() and just wrapping your replications in a parallel statement like parallel::parLappy() instead (its more efficient). 

Phil

messages.author: f532f98b3e9b7d93
messages.subject: Re: mirtCluster() in Linux
parts:
Hi Phil,

I don't have any specific example but using the LSAT7 data, I got the following results:

data<-expand.table(LSAT7)

d<-cbind(data,data,data) # just to make it larger

colnames(d)<-paste('item',1:15,sep='')

- without executing mirtCluster()

m<-mirt(d,1,method='MHRM')  #MHRM terminated after 2000 iterations

  user  system elapsed
 55.169   0.448  55.674


- with executing mirtCluster()

   user  system elapsed
 43.689   1.210 141.920

The time-consuming piece was the calculation of log-likelihoods. Here are the specification of the Linux that I'm using:

https://www.usask.ca/ict/services/research-technologies/advanced-computing/meton/index.php


And here the result of the same analysis on a Windows 7 machine with 8 cores and 12 GB of RAM:

-without executing mirtCluster()

 user  system elapsed 
  40.05    0.08   40.31 

- with executing mirtCluster()

  user  system elapsed 
  29.70    0.29   40.37

I'm not sure what's going on. Any thoughts?

Thanks.

parts:
Interesting, I get the same thing on my 48 core server running ubuntu as well: 

> library(mirt)
Loading required package: stats4
Loading required package: lattice

> data<-expand.table(LSAT7)
> 
> d<-cbind(data,data,data) # just to make it larger
> 
> colnames(d)<-paste('item',1:15,sep='')

> m<-mirt(d,1,method='MHRM')
Stage 3 = 2000, LL = -6813.0, AR(4.60) = [0.20], gam = 0.0006, Max-Change = 0.0116
MHRM terminated after 2000 iterations.

Calculating log-likelihood...
> extract.mirt(m, 'time')
   TOTAL     DATA ESTIMATE MH_draws    Mstep       SE     POST 
  39.348    0.082   29.761   25.615    3.732    0.000    9.503 
> mirtCluster()
> m2<-mirt(d,1,method='MHRM')
Stage 3 = 2000, LL = -6813.0, AR(4.60) = [0.20], gam = 0.0006, Max-Change = 0.0116
MHRM terminated after 2000 iterations.

Calculating log-likelihood...
> extract.mirt(m2, 'time')
   TOTAL     DATA ESTIMATE MH_draws    Mstep       SE     POST 
  98.390    0.058   28.096   24.206    3.601    0.000   70.236 
> mirtCluster(remove=TRUE)
> mirtCluster(
spec=    ...=     remove=  
> mirtCluster(2)
> m3<-mirt(d,1,method='MHRM')
Stage 3 = 2000, LL = -6813.0, AR(4.60) = [0.20], gam = 0.0006, Max-Change = 0.0116
MHRM terminated after 2000 iterations.

Calculating log-likelihood...
> extract.mirt(m3, 'time')
   TOTAL     DATA ESTIMATE MH_draws    Mstep       SE     POST 
  36.473    0.058   28.194   24.304    3.636    0.000    8.220 


Looks like there is diminishing returns when defining the parallel operations this way. I'll look into whether there is a better way, but for now I'd recommend not using it (or dropping the number of cores required because R's socket splitting approach seems to have data-transferring issues). 

Phil

messages.author: 6a75f6f91a59c568
messages.subject: Re: mirtCluster() in Linux
parts:
Hi,

In my knowledge, The MRO doesn't allow 48 thread. If you have 12 physical core, MRO may recognize just 12 core.

I'm using HP Z600 Workstation X5650 with Ubuntu 16.04 + OpenBLAS. It works well than Ubuntu 16.04 + MRO. In MRO Ubuntu Linux version, Intel Math Kernel Library will load as packages like snow or parallel, not native in Windows. It may cause mirtCluster() function will not run well.

Seongho Bae

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: mirtCluster() in Linux
parts:
I've talked to Matthias about this, and in mirt this seems very unlikely. Optimizing the M-step in particular would be very ineffective because of mirt's use of R's optimizers, which only run on single cores. Plus, the customized IRT models that can be written would be extremely painful to parallelize because the code is written in pure R rather than compiled code. 

I think if I were to write a different version of the package, possibly in a language like Julia, then this type of customization would seem more plausible. 

Phil

library(parallel)

ncores = detectCores()
cl = makeCluster(ncores)

wait <- function(i){
    Sys.sleep(1)
    invisible(NULL)
}

# this should take 10 seconds
#system.time(lapply(1:ncores, wait))

# this should take less time depending on the number of cores you have
system.time(parLapply(cl, 1:ncores, wait))


# when you're all done
stopCluster(cl)

I think if I were to write a different version of the package, possibly in a language like Julia, then this type of customization would seem more plausible.
